newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED MIXED ON FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED MIXED ON FRIDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in fairly thin trade on Friday.
Local money dealers said they expected the rates to start trending upwards in the wake of a recent rise in annual inflation, which went up to 22.4 percent in April from 19.9 percent in March.

The March figure, which was another rise from 19 percent the previous month, saw the rates surging to around 23 percent from 16 percent in the space of four weeks and dealers said the pattern was likely to be repeated.

On Friday, the central Reserve Bank carried out an auction for treasury bills worth Z$600 million at an average yield of 22.61 percent. By midday, the results of a second auction for Z$800 million treasury bills were still pending.
NCD bills with 30-, 60- and 90-day maturities were quoted at 25 percent (buying) from 24 percent while their selling rate ranged from 19 to 20 percent from 23 percent.
Bankers acceptances were being bought and sold at 23 and 21.5 percent respctively from 23.5 and 22.75 percent with call money quoted steady at 19 percent.
